messages.subject: Two datasets with two legends?
parts:
Hi!

I am plotting a dataset and adding geom_vline from a second dataset to mark certain actions in time. However, I was unable to find out how to get the legends related to geom_vline and the second dataset.

I'm using something similar to that, execpt that I'm using time as x axis. I would like to have at least a legend with "Action" in the "y2" dataset. Should I include y2 in a melted y1?

Thank you all!

guillaume

-

y1 = data.frame(A = c(1:100), B = rnorm(100), C = rnorm(100), D = rnorm(100))
y1.m = melt(y1, id="A")

y2 = data.frame(.A. = c(10, 50, 80), Press = c(NA, 2 , 3), Action = c(".a.",".b.",".c."))

p = ggplot(y1.m , aes(x=A, y=value, color=variable)) +
         geom_vline(data=y2, aes(xintercept=.A., linetype=Action, alpha=Press)) +
         geom_point() +         
         facet_grid(variable ~ ., scale="free_y")
p

parts:
Hi:

Something seems wrong, as I would have expected a legend for linetype. I did a little fiddling around (thanks for the reproducible example, BTW) and it's clear that ggplot2 is not rendering the legend for linetypes coming from geom_vline() with the 'usual' mantra:

y1 = data.frame(A = c(1:100), B = rnorm(100), C = rnorm(100), D = rnorm(100))
y1.m = melt(y1, id="A")

y2 = data.frame(.A. = c(10, 50, 80), Press = c(NA, 2 , 3), Action = c(".a.",".b.",".c."))

> str(y2)
'data.frame':   3 obs. of  3 variables:
 $ .A.   : num  10 50 80
 $ Press : num  NA 2 3
 $ Action: Factor w/ 3 levels ".a.",".b.",".c.": 1 2 3

# => Action seems OK as an aesthetic for linetype.
# To simplify matters,
y2$A <- y2[[".A."]]    # copy .A. to A

# Reformulate the call so that A is the only 
# common aesthetic among layers, since A is now in both 
# y1.m and y2.  No legend for linetype appears.
ggplot(y1.m, aes(x = A)) +
  geom_vline(data = y2, aes(xintercept = A, linetype = Action)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = value, color = variable)) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ ., scale = "free_y")

# Try to make an explicit legend for linetype...no change.
# (Ditto for scale_linetype_discrete().)
last_plot() + scale_linetype(breaks = levels(y2$Action))

# Redoing the plot and using scale_linetype_manual()
# doesn't help, either:
ggplot(y1.m, aes(x = A)) +
  geom_vline(data = y2, aes(xintercept = A, linetype = Action)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = value, color = variable)) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ ., scale = "free_y") +
  scale_linetype_manual(breaks = levels(y2$Action), values = 1:3)

messages.subject: Re: Two datasets with two legends?
parts:
Hi Dennis and all!

I've played around with the plot and the problem seems to come from geom_vline and the second data frame, and not the legend for linetype. A legend is generated for the main dataset, but none is generated for geom_vline and the second dataset.

y1 = data.frame(A = c(1:100), B = rnorm(100), C = rnorm(100), D = rnorm(100))
y1.m = melt(y1, id="A")
y2 = data.frame(.A. = c(10, 50, 80), Press = c(NA, 2 , 3), Action = c(".a.",".b.",".c."))
y2$A <- y2[[".A."]]    # copy .A. to A
# This generates a legend for color in geom_point:

ggplot(y1.m, aes(x = A)) +
  geom_vline(data = y2, aes(xintercept = A, linetype = Action)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = value, color = variable)) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ ., scale = "free_y")
# This generates a legend for linetype in geom_line (here replacing geom_point in the previous example):
ggplot(y1.m, aes(x = A)) +

geom_vline(data = y2, aes(xintercept = A, color = Action)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = value, linetype = variable)) +
facet_grid(variable ~ ., scale = "free_y")

Is that a bug? Is there a workaround? Is the problem with geom_vline or with a second dataset?

Thank you!

guillaume

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Two datasets with two legends?
parts:
Hi guys,

It really is a good idea to read the docs:

?geom_vline

Arguments:
show_guide: should a legend be drawn? (defaults to ‘FALSE’)

So we need

ggplot(y1.m , aes(x=A, y=value, color=variable)) +
geom_vline(data=y2, aes(xintercept=.A., linetype=Action,
alpha=Press), show_guide=TRUE) +

geom_point() +
facet_grid(variable ~ ., scale="free_y")

Best,
Ista
